title: The Panama Canal lifts ships 26 metres without a single pump
body: Ships crossing Panama are raised about 26 metres to Gatun Lake, an artificial lake made by damming the Chagres River, then lowered again on the other side. The original locks need no pumps: valves open and lake water flows downhill through large tunnels into each chamber, lifting the ship. The catch is that every transit sends huge amounts of fresh water out to sea, which is why droughts can force limits on traffic.
